answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works like a trellis guiding a vine: every new identity must lock its own bond, so a thousand cloned bots must lock a thousand distinct bonds. Payouts are priced by verified output, not account count, so extra clones earn near nothing yet each still parks collateral. Fraud burns the bond via slashing along with the reputation bound to that key, which cannot move to a fresh wallet. The cost curve rises faster than sybil yield: every fake agent costs a full bond and may forfeit it, and an onyx wall of duplicates never beats one pearl of settled work.
